fix.shows: Frontline reports estimates by Sankalp, a political research consultancy in Karnataka, of how the fall in Karnataka's roll divides by religion. The roll does not record religion, and the magazine says Sankalp's figures by religion are estimates. Karnataka's roll fell from 5.54 crore electors before the revision to 4.55 crore on the final roll, or 17.9 per cent. By Sankalp's estimate Muslim electors fell from 71.56 lakh to 58.08 lakh, or 18.84 per cent, and other electors from 4.82 crore to 3.96 crore, or 17.79 per cent, so the Muslim share of the roll went from 12.91 per cent to 12.77 per cent. In Bengaluru's 28 seats the roll fell from 1.03 crore to 59.08 lakh, and Sankalp puts the fall at 33.72 per cent for Muslim electors and 43.82 per cent for others. In the other 196 seats it puts the fall at 15.32 per cent for Muslim electors and 12.18 per cent for others. The political analyst Sandeep Shastri tells the magazine that Bengaluru's roll had long been inflated by electors living abroad or voting in their home towns. Of the 1,07,96,339 names left off the draft, Sankalp estimates that 15.43 lakh were of Muslim electors and 92.32 lakh of others. It also counts 39 of the 224 seats where booths that gave 60 per cent or more of their votes in the 2024 Lok Sabha election to the Congress hold more than 35 per cent of the seat's names left off the draft. Across those 39 seats 42 per cent of the names left off are in such booths, and 26 of the seats are held by the Congress, 11 by the BJP and 2 by the Janata Dal (Secular). Frontline reports, from sources in the office of Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer, that 716 foreign nationals were found on the roll, 641 of them from Nepal.
